articles.title: Weather on the board today
articles.body:
A dense high-pressure system of caste resentment dominated the board, pinning down the Delhi model debates and surname shaming in a thick, stagnant air.

The weight was heavy, and visibility was poor for hours as the usual squalls of tribalism broke over the capital's image. A brief cold snap of mathematical pretension moved through the morning.

One anon claimed OpenAI had brute-forced the Hodge Conjecture with raw compute, a front that quickly dissipated into skepticism and confusion. Simultaneously, a sudden heat wave of national pride surged from the west.

Anon posted heart emojis for Islamabad's infrastructure, a warm front that warmed the board for a few minutes before the ambient hostility returned. Low cloud cover of petty personal logistics settled in the evening.

Driving lessons and foreign woman acquisition plans drifted across the screen, thin and unremarkable, before the day's thick atmosphere slowly dispersed.

articles.title: Anons Debounce Delhi Models and Caste Surnames
articles.body:
Anons spent the day mocking Delhi-based influencers and arguing over the ethnic origins of specific surnames. The thread centered on Instagram accounts of young women, with posters describing them as performative and mocking their physical attributes.

One anon shared a link to an influencer named Pranjal Priya, describing her as a "Delhi ki stacyjeeta" who does a bikini rampwalk in Miss India competitions.

The poster called it a "performative naatak" reel designed to appease family while serving as "modern high school delhi ki randi" content. Another user claimed to have coomed twice to the specific girl posted, ignoring arguments about her identity.

A respondent stated they only cared about the original post and dismissed other links as irrelevant to their "coom session." The discussion shifted to other accounts, including one named Di Tanwar. Anons debated whether Tanwar was a Rajput or Gujjar surname.

One poster claimed Tomar was the Rajput clan name and Tanwar was its Gujjar appropriation, using it as a last name.

Another counter-argued that Tomar was a Rajput surname and Tanwar was a different entity, telling the first poster to search online. A third anon mocked a user for "cope"-ing, stating that girls of the respondent's caste were the biggest "randi" anyway.

Physical descriptions dominated the replies. One user described finding a video of a "tall jaatni" changing clothes, noting her "saggy boobs" and admitting to cooming. Another insisted Pranjal Priya's breasts were "top tier" and not saggy.

A third poster claimed the influencer had undergone surgery at age 18, saying her life was "set hai." Another anon noted the girl had three or four similar influencers with private Instagram accounts, expressing frustration at the abundance of "stacy" type content.

A user identified as "वे" interjected to ask for more video content, stating they were playing The Witcher and would post more in the evening.

Another anon replied that they did not have many videos of that type and asked "वे" to post some. "वे" later sent a goodnight message, noting that it was almost 4 AM.

The thread concluded with mixed claims about caste identities, with one user asking if Pranjal Priya was Bamani, only to be told they did not care because they intended to coom.

articles.title: Anon Claims OpenAI Solved Hodge Conjecture via Compute
articles.body:
Anon asserted that OpenAI had likely solved the Hodge conjecture, a millennium problem.

The poster argued that the breakthrough was less about new mathematical insight and more about brute force computation, suggesting that hiring mathematicians and granting them access to large internal models is all that was required.

Another respondent supported this engineering paradigm view, citing Demis Hassabis winning a Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold. This anon argued that computer scientists solving domain-specific problems now defines a new era, comparing the current shift to the industrial revolution.

They maintained that lives would change fundamentally, noting that the era currently lacks a proper name but is effectively irreversible. Skeptics pushed back on the timeline.

One anon stated that for problems like the Riemann Hypothesis or P vs NP, elite mathematicians insist entirely new fields of mathematics are required, making a solution by the end of the year unlikely.

However, the same poster conceded that who knows what the decade might bring.

Another anon took a more dismissive tone, replying that by the end of the year, all open math problems might get solved because it was just a compute issue all along. The thread turned to the reaction of the mathematical community.

One poster asked if the "mathchud" had seethed on Xitter, describing it as the biggest crashout ever. Another confirmed that even Terence Tao, who had dedicated years to the Navier-Stokes problem, was seething.

The consensus was that the established order was shaking, though one anon expressed fear that the rapid changes could worsen existing situations, while another insisted the next step was obviously cyborg technology and acceleration.

The discussion concluded with a mix of resignation and identity politics.

One anon accused a respondent of being a "low IQ kike worshipping gooner pajeet" for expressing doubt, to which the target replied that they were not the anon previously associated with lean and spiritual AI.

A final poster simply labeled the exchange a "high IQ thread," ending the exchange with a nod to the perceived intellectual superiority of the group.

articles.title: Heartbroken Anon Defends Islamabad Infrastructure
articles.body:
Anon posted a twenty-three-megabyte image of Islamabad with three heart emojis, expressing affection for the Pakistani capital.

The image featured a wide, clean avenue lined with trees, a view that immediately divided the board between those who found it aesthetically pleasing and those who focused on geopolitical grievances.

The first reply linked to a YouTube playlist, providing additional context for the urban landscape. Another Anon noted that the city is the first result for Islamabad on Google Images, suggesting its visual dominance in search queries.

This observation was met with a reply calling the OP a likely admin, though no further evidence was provided to support the accusation.

A respondent argued unironically that Pakistan is a better place to live than India, claiming Islamabad looks like the most civilised city in South Asia.

This sentiment was countered by another Anon who described the land as stolen but admitted the image looked absolutely kino. The aesthetic appreciation persisted despite the political disagreement, with one user noting that the visual quality was undeniable regardless of ownership claims.

The conversation took a darker turn when an Anon mentioned the city's proximity to the Jammu border, suggesting it would be fun to bomb the infrastructure there. A reply to this suggestion dismissed the bomber as a barbarian who always remains a barbarian.

The thread did not attempt to de-escalate this specific comment, leaving the violent proposal standing as a stark contrast to the initial emotional attachment to the city's beauty. The discussion eventually shifted to the source of the love.

One Anon downplayed the affection, stating they did not love Pakistan that much and identifying as Sindhi. Another user compared the praise to what Indians say about their own infrastructure, implying a shared pattern of nationalistic self-congratulation.

The thread ended with a cryptic reply simply stating "dyaush," refusing to engage further with the debate over civilisation and conflict.

articles.title: Driving Lessons and Bussy Advice
articles.body:
Anon announced he is taking driving lessons. The replies quickly devolved into a mix of practical advice and obscene trolling.

One poster claimed their instructor speaks in broken English, shouting commands like "kilach dabao" while making the student want to bash his head against the steering wheel.

A user named yellow rose advised not to shove the gear shifter in his bussy, claiming he learned that the hard way. He followed up by asking people to bookmark his website for naked bussy content.

Other Anons suggested treating every driver as a potential retard, staying fifty meters away from rickshaws, and assuming all bikers are chimps who ignore indicators.
